title: Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe: the lame man healed + mistaken for Zeus and Hermes; Paul stoned

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass in Iconium that they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spake that a great multitude both of Jews and of Greeks believed.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν Ἰκονίῳ κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ λαλῆσαι οὕτως ὥστε πιστεῦσαι Ἰουδαίων τε καὶ Ἑλλήνων πολὺ πλῆθος.
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de en Ikoniō kata to auto eiselthein autous eis tēn synagōgēn tōn Ioudaiōn kai lalēsai houtōs hōste pisteusai Ioudaiōn te kai Hellēnōn poly plēthos.

paragraphs.text: But the Jews that were disobedient stirred up the souls of the Gentiles, and made them evil affected against the brethren.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἀπειθήσαντες Ἰουδαῖοι ἐπήγειραν καὶ ἐκάκωσαν τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de apeithēsantes Ioudaioi epēgeiran kai ekakōsan tas psychas tōn ethnōn kata tōn adelphōn.

paragraphs.text: Long time therefore they tarried [there] speaking boldly in the Lord, who bare witness unto the word of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
paragraphs.original: ἱκανὸν μὲν οὖν χρόνον διέτριψαν παρρησιαζόμενοι ἐπὶ τῷ κυρίῳ τῷ μαρτυροῦντι τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, διδόντι σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hikanon men oun chronon dietripsan parrēsiazomenoi epi tō kyriō tō martyrounti tō logō tēs charitos autou, didonti sēmeia kai terata ginesthai dia tōn cheirōn autōn.

paragraphs.text: But the multitude of the city was divided; and part held with the Jews, and part with the apostles.
paragraphs.original: ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ πλῆθος τῆς πόλεως, καὶ οἱ μὲν ἦσαν σὺν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις οἱ δὲ σὺν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις.
paragraphs.translit: eschisthē de to plēthos tēs poleōs, kai hoi men ēsan syn tois Ioudaiois hoi de syn tois apostolois.

paragraphs.text: And when there was made an onset both of the Gentiles and of the Jews with their rulers, to treat them shamefully and to stone them,
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ὁρμὴ τῶν ἐθνῶν τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων σὺν τοῖς ἄρχουσιν αὐτῶν ὑβρίσαι καὶ λιθοβολῆσαι αὐτούς,
paragraphs.translit: hōs de egeneto hormē tōn ethnōn te kai Ioudaiōn syn tois archousin autōn hybrisai kai lithobolēsai autous,

paragraphs.text: they became aware of it, and fled unto the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and the region round about:
paragraphs.original: συνιδόντες κατέφυγον εἰς τὰς πόλεις τῆς Λυκαονίας Λύστραν καὶ Δέρβην καὶ τὴν περίχωρον,
paragraphs.translit: synidontes katephygon eis tas poleis tēs Lykaonias Lystran kai Derbēn kai tēn perichōron,

paragraphs.text: and there they preached the gospel.
paragraphs.original: κἀκεῖ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ἦσαν.
paragraphs.translit: kakei euangelizomenoi ēsan.

paragraphs.text: And at Lystra there sat a certain man, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother`s womb, who never had walked.
paragraphs.original: Καί τις ἀνὴρ ἀδύνατος ἐν Λύστροις τοῖς ποσὶν ἐκάθητο, χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ, ὃς οὐδέποτε περιεπάτησεν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai tis anēr adynatos en Lystrois tois posin ekathēto, chōlos ek koilias mētros autou, hos oudepote periepatēsen.

paragraphs.text: The same heard Paul speaking, who, fastening eyes upon him, and seeing that he had faith to be made whole,
paragraphs.original: οὗτος ἤκουσεν τοῦ Παύλου λαλοῦντος· ὃς ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἰδὼν ὅτι ἔχει πίστιν τοῦ σωθῆναι
paragraphs.translit: houtos ēkousen tou Paulou lalountos· hos atenisas autō kai idōn hoti echei pistin tou sōthēnai

paragraphs.text: said with a loud voice, Stand upright on thy feet. And he leaped up and walked.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν μεγάλῃ φωνῇ· Ἀνάστηθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου ὀρθός· καὶ ἥλατο καὶ περιεπάτει.
paragraphs.translit: eipen megalē phōnē· Anastēthi epi tous podas sou orthos· kai hēlato kai periepatei.

paragraphs.text: And when the multitude saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voice, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men.
paragraphs.original: οἵ τε ὄχλοι ἰδόντες ὃ ἐποίησεν Παῦλος ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν Λυκαονιστὶ λέγοντες· Οἱ θεοὶ ὁμοιωθέντες ἀνθρώποις κατέβησαν πρὸς ἡμᾶς
paragraphs.translit: hoi te ochloi idontes ho epoiēsen Paulos epēran tēn phōnēn autōn Lykaonisti legontes· Hoi theoi homoiōthentes anthrōpois katebēsan pros hēmas

paragraphs.text: And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercury, because he was the chief speaker.
paragraphs.original: ἐκάλουν τε τὸν Βαρναβᾶν Δία, τὸν δὲ Παῦλον Ἑρμῆν, ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ ἡγούμενος τοῦ λόγου.
paragraphs.translit: ekaloun te ton Barnaban Dia, ton de Paulon Hermēn, epeidē autos ēn ho hēgoumenos tou logou.

paragraphs.text: And the priest of Jupiter whose [temple] was before the city, brought oxen and garlands unto the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the multitudes.
paragraphs.original: ὅ τε ἱερεὺς τοῦ Διὸς τοῦ ὄντος πρὸ τῆς πόλεως ταύρους καὶ στέμματα ἐπὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας ἐνέγκας σὺν τοῖς ὄχλοις ἤθελεν θύειν.
paragraphs.translit: ho te hiereus tou Dios tou ontos pro tēs poleōs taurous kai stemmata epi tous pylōnas enenkas syn tois ochlois ēthelen thyein.

paragraphs.text: But when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of it, they rent their garments, and sprang forth among the multitude, crying out
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι Βαρναβᾶς καὶ Παῦλος, διαρρήξαντες τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν ἐξεπήδησαν εἰς τὸν ὄχλον κράζοντες
paragraphs.translit: akousantes de hoi apostoloi Barnabas kai Paulos, diarrēxantes ta himatia autōn exepēdēsan eis ton ochlon krazontes

paragraphs.text: and saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and bring you good tidings, that ye should turn from these vain things unto a living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea, and all that in them is:
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγοντες· Ἄνδρες, τί ταῦτα ποιεῖτε; καὶ ἡμεῖς ὁμοιοπαθεῖς ἐσμεν ὑμῖν ἄνθρωποι, εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τούτων τῶν ματαίων ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ θεὸν ζῶντα ὃς ἐποίησεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: kai legontes· Andres, ti tauta poieite; kai hēmeis homoiopatheis esmen hymin anthrōpoi, euangelizomenoi hymas apo toutōn tōn mataiōn epistrephein epi theon zōnta hos epoiēsen ton ouranon kai tēn gēn kai tēn thalassan kai panta ta en autois·

paragraphs.text: who in the generations gone by suffered all the nations to walk in their own ways.
paragraphs.original: ὃς ἐν ταῖς παρῳχημέναις γενεαῖς εἴασεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πορεύεσθαι ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν·
paragraphs.translit: hos en tais parōchēmenais geneais eiasen panta ta ethnē poreuesthai tais hodois autōn·

paragraphs.text: And yet He left not himself without witness, in that he did good and gave you from heaven rains and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.
paragraphs.original: καίτοι οὐκ ἀμάρτυρον αὑτὸν ἀφῆκεν ἀγαθουργῶν, οὐρανόθεν ὑμῖν ὑετοὺς διδοὺς καὶ καιροὺς καρποφόρους, ἐμπιπλῶν τροφῆς καὶ εὐφροσύνης τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kaitoi ouk amartyron hauton aphēken agathourgōn, ouranothen hymin hyetous didous kai kairous karpophorous, empiplōn trophēs kai euphrosynēs tas kardias hymōn.

paragraphs.text: And with these sayings scarce restrained they the multitudes from doing sacrifice unto them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντες μόλις κατέπαυσαν τοὺς ὄχλους τοῦ μὴ θύειν αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: kai tauta legontes molis katepausan tous ochlous tou mē thyein autois.

paragraphs.text: But there came Jews thither from Antioch and Iconium: and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul, and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.
paragraphs.original: Ἐπῆλθαν δὲ ἀπὸ Ἀντιοχείας καὶ Ἰκονίου Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ πείσαντες τοὺς ὄχλους καὶ λιθάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον ἔσυρον ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, νομίζοντες αὐτὸν τεθνηκέναι.
paragraphs.translit: Epēlthan de apo Antiocheias kai Ikoniou Ioudaioi, kai peisantes tous ochlous kai lithasantes ton Paulon esyron exō tēs poleōs, nomizontes auton tethnēkenai.

paragraphs.text: But as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and entered into the city: and on the morrow he went forth with Barnabas to Derbe.
paragraphs.original: κυκλωσάντων δὲ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτὸν ἀναστὰς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν. καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τῷ Βαρναβᾷ εἰς Δέρβην.
paragraphs.translit: kyklōsantōn de tōn mathētōn auton anastas eisēlthen eis tēn polin. kai tē epaurion exēlthen syn tō Barnaba eis Derbēn.

paragraphs.text: And when they had preached the gospel to that city, and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, and to Iconium, and to Antioch,
paragraphs.original: Εὐαγγελισάμενοί τε τὴν πόλιν ἐκείνην καὶ μαθητεύσαντες ἱκανοὺς ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Λύστραν καὶ εἰς Ἰκόνιον καὶ εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν,
paragraphs.translit: Euangelisamenoi te tēn polin ekeinēn kai mathēteusantes hikanous hypestrepsan eis tēn Lystran kai eis Ikonion kai eis Antiocheian,

paragraphs.text: confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God.
paragraphs.original: ἐπιστηρίζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν μαθητῶν, παρακαλοῦντες ἐμμένειν τῇ πίστει καὶ ὅτι διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων δεῖ ἡμᾶς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: epistērizontes tas psychas tōn mathētōn, parakalountes emmenein tē pistei kai hoti dia pollōn thlipseōn dei hēmas eiselthein eis tēn basileian tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And when they had appointed for them elders in every church, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they had believed.
paragraphs.original: χειροτονήσαντες δὲ αὐτοῖς κατʼ ἐκκλησίαν πρεσβυτέρους προσευξάμενοι μετὰ νηστειῶν παρέθεντο αὐτοὺς τῷ κυρίῳ εἰς ὃν πεπιστεύκεισαν.
paragraphs.translit: cheirotonēsantes de autois katʼ ekklēsian presbyterous proseuxamenoi meta nēsteiōn parethento autous tō kyriō eis hon pepisteukeisan.

paragraphs.text: And they passed through Pisidia, and came to Pamphylia.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διελθόντες τὴν Πισιδίαν ἦλθον εἰς τὴν Παμφυλίαν,
paragraphs.translit: kai dielthontes tēn Pisidian ēlthon eis tēn Pamphylian,

paragraphs.text: And when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia;
paragraphs.original: καὶ λαλήσαντες ἐν Πέργῃ τὸν λόγον κατέβησαν εἰς Ἀττάλειαν,
paragraphs.translit: kai lalēsantes en Pergē ton logon katebēsan eis Attaleian,

paragraphs.text: and thence they sailed to Antioch, from whence they had been committed to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled.
paragraphs.original: κἀκεῖθεν ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, ὅθεν ἦσαν παραδεδομένοι τῇ χάριτι τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ ἐπλήρωσαν.
paragraphs.translit: kakeithen apepleusan eis Antiocheian, hothen ēsan paradedomenoi tē chariti tou theou eis to ergon ho eplērōsan.

paragraphs.text: And when they were come, and had gathered the church together, they rehearsed all things that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith unto the Gentiles.
paragraphs.original: παραγενόμενοι δὲ καὶ συναγαγόντες τὴν ἐκκλησίαν ἀνήγγελλον ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς μετʼ αὐτῶν καὶ ὅτι ἤνοιξεν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν θύραν πίστεως.
paragraphs.translit: paragenomenoi de kai synagagontes tēn ekklēsian anēngellon hosa epoiēsen ho theos metʼ autōn kai hoti ēnoixen tois ethnesin thyran pisteōs.

paragraphs.text: And they tarried no little time with the disciples.
paragraphs.original: διέτριβον δὲ χρόνον οὐκ ὀλίγον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς.
paragraphs.translit: dietribon de chronon ouk oligon syn tois mathētais.
